title: Indira Gandhi Pyari Behna Sukh Samman Nidhi Yojana
meta_description: Indira Gandhi Pyari Behna Sukh Samman Nidhi Yojana provides Rs 1,500/month to women in Himachal Pradesh. Eligibility, how to apply, and DBT payment details.

hero.one_liner: Indira Gandhi Pyari Behna Sukh Samman Nidhi Yojana gives Rs 1,500 a month to eligible women in Himachal Pradesh by DBT. Launched February 2024.

what_is_it: The Indira Gandhi Pyari Behna Sukh Samman Nidhi Yojana was launched on February 25, 2024 by Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu to provide regular financial support to women in the state. The scheme delivers Rs 1,500 per month directly to the bank accounts of eligible women aged 18 to 59 years, creating a source of personal income that does not depend on employment or family circumstances.

The scheme takes its name from former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and reflects the state government's commitment to women's economic empowerment through direct cash transfers. Himachal Pradesh has a large rural population spread across mountainous terrain where women's economic participation in formal employment remains limited, making a regular monthly transfer particularly meaningful for household financial security.

Excludes government employees, pensioners, and income-tax payers. Apply via the Tehsil Welfare Officer. At 60, women transition to the state old age pension.

how_to_apply.title: Gather Documents
how_to_apply.description: Collect your Aadhaar card, a Himachal Pradesh domicile certificate or residence proof, your bank passbook showing the account linked to Aadhaar, and an income certificate for the family from the Tehsildar confirming annual family income is below Rs 2 lakh.

how_to_apply.title: Visit the Block Development Office or Anganwadi Centre
how_to_apply.description: Go to the nearest Block Development Office (BDO) or Anganwadi centre in your area; Anganwadi workers and ASHA workers have been designated as registration facilitators and can help you fill the application form and verify your eligibility.

how_to_apply.title: Submit the Application Form
how_to_apply.description: Fill the Pyari Behna Sukh Samman Nidhi application form and submit it along with copies of your Aadhaar card, income certificate, domicile certificate, and bank passbook; the form is available at the BDO office and at Anganwadi centres.

how_to_apply.title: Aadhaar-Bank Linkage Verification
how_to_apply.description: The BDO office verifies that your bank account is Aadhaar-linked and DBT-enabled before approving the application; if your account is not yet linked, get it linked at the bank branch or through the Aadhaar portal and then return for verification.

how_to_apply.title: Wait for Approval and First Payment
how_to_apply.description: After submission, the district Women and Child Development office processes the application and adds approved beneficiaries to the monthly payment list; once approved, you will receive an SMS on your registered mobile number and the Rs 1,500 will be credited directly to your bank account in the next payment cycle.

ministry: Women and Child Development Department, Himachal Pradesh

extra_sections.heading: What the Pyari Behna Scheme Is
content: Women who receive the Rs 1,500 monthly payment are free to use it as they see fit, whether for household essentials, children's education, medical expenses, or small personal savings; this unconditional nature of the transfer distinguishes it from tied benefits that require specific expenditure patterns. The income also gives women greater negotiating power within the household by providing them with a resource they control directly.

The scheme is funded from the Himachal Pradesh state budget and administered through the Women and Child Development Department, which maintains a centralised database of beneficiaries linked to the state's social welfare management systems. Registration and verification are done at the sub-divisional or block level, and payments are released monthly through the DBT mechanism.

extra_sections.heading: What the Pyari Behna Scheme Is More
content: Himachal Pradesh implemented this scheme as part of a broader social security agenda that includes other direct transfer programmes for different sections of the population; the Pyari Behna scheme specifically targets women in the working-age group of 18 to 59, who are often left out of pension schemes designed for elderly beneficiaries. By targeting this age bracket, the government aims to support women during the productive years of their lives when economic security has the greatest impact on family welfare.

The state government has sought to ensure that the scheme reaches women in remote hill areas by processing applications and payments through the district and block administrative machinery rather than requiring beneficiaries to travel to state capital offices. This decentralised approach has extended the reach of the scheme to women living in far-flung panchayats in districts such as Kinnaur, Lahaul and Spiti, and Chamba.

extra_sections.title: A Monthly Income for HP Women
extra_sections.content:
Launched on 25 February 2024 by CM Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, this scheme gives eligible women in Himachal Pradesh Rs 1,500 a month. The money is theirs to use as they wish.

It is one of the state's election guarantees, aimed at giving women in hill households a steady, independent income.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible
content: Women belonging to scheduled caste and scheduled tribe communities in Himachal Pradesh have been encouraged to register for the Pyari Behna scheme alongside existing SC/ST-specific welfare programmes, as the income limit criterion of Rs 2 lakh family income per year aligns well with the economic profile of many tribal households. The scheme does not restrict eligibility by caste, making it a universal women's income support programme within the specified age and income bands.

The monthly payment of Rs 1,500, while modest, provides a meaningful supplement to household income in rural Himachal Pradesh where the cost of essentials in hill areas can be high; for many women in subsistence farming households, this represents the first time they have a regular personal income in their own name. Field reports from the initial rollout suggested that a large proportion of early registrants were women who had previously had no personal income whatsoever.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible More
content: The Pyari Behna scheme requires beneficiaries to maintain an Aadhaar-linked and DBT-enabled bank account, which has also served as an incentive for financial inclusion among women who had not previously held individual bank accounts. Block-level officials and Anganwadi workers have assisted women in opening accounts at nearby bank branches or through the India Post Payments Bank network where commercial bank branches are distant.

The scheme does not require beneficiaries to perform any specific activity or meet any ongoing condition beyond maintaining their bank account and updating their Aadhaar linkage; it is a pure unconditional income transfer. This design reduces the administrative burden on both the government and the beneficiary, and ensures that women engaged in domestic work or care roles are not excluded on grounds that they cannot demonstrate formal employment.

extra_sections.heading: The Income and Exclusion Rules
content: An important exclusion criterion is that women employed in any government service or receiving a government pension are not eligible for the Pyari Behna scheme, as such women already receive a regular income from the state. Similarly, income tax payers and their family members are excluded, as the scheme is designed for economically weaker sections of the population who do not have access to formal employment-based income.

The state government has set up a helpline and grievance mechanism for beneficiaries who have not received their monthly payment or whose registration has been rejected; women can contact the block development office or the Women and Child Development Department's district office to resolve issues. The department also conducts periodic reviews of the beneficiary list to update records where a woman has become ineligible due to changed circumstances.

extra_sections.heading: The Income and Exclusion Rules More
content: Each registered beneficiary typically receives a payment in the first or second week of the month for the preceding month, subject to the state's budget release cycle; occasional delays may occur when the treasury release is pending, but the government has committed to clearing arrears promptly. Women who experience non-receipt of payment in a given month should wait a few extra days before contacting the block office, as processing timelines can vary.

The Pyari Behna scheme has drawn comparisons with similar women's income support programmes in other states such as Jharkhand's Mukhyamantri Maiya Samman Yojana and Madhya Pradesh's Ladli Behna Yojana, all of which use DBT to deliver Rs 1,000 to Rs 1,500 per month to women; Himachal Pradesh's scheme is part of this emerging national trend of state governments providing direct income support to women as a social security measure. The proliferation of such schemes reflects a growing recognition that women's economic security requires targeted support beyond what general poverty-alleviation programmes provide.

extra_sections.title: Paid Directly to Your Account
extra_sections.desc:
The payment is made by DBT to your Aadhaar-linked bank account, usually in the first or second week of the month.

Keep your Aadhaar seeded to your bank, or the payment can fail even after approval. Check your status if a month's payment does not arrive.

extra_sections.heading: How to Apply
content: Himachal Pradesh has also linked the Pyari Behna registration drive with awareness about other state welfare programmes, so women who register for the monthly stipend may also receive information about HIMCARE health insurance, Mukhyamantri Baal Ashirwad Yojana, and other programmes they may be entitled to. This bundled outreach approach helps maximise the uptake of available benefits among women who were previously unaware of schemes they could access.

The Women and Child Development Department works closely with Panchayati Raj institutions and Gram Panchayat secretaries to identify potential beneficiaries in each village, particularly women who are not connected with Anganwadi centres and who might otherwise miss the registration window. Village-level camps have been organised in multiple districts to facilitate on-the-spot registration, document verification, and Aadhaar-bank linkage checking in one place, reducing the burden on women who would otherwise need multiple trips to block offices.

extra_sections.heading: How to Apply More
content: For women who are self-employed in home-based occupations such as weaving, knitting, pickle making, or rearing poultry, the Rs 1,500 monthly credit can function as working capital supplementation rather than mere consumption support; some beneficiaries in Kangra and Mandi districts have reported using the accumulated monthly payments to purchase raw materials in bulk at lower prices, improving their small enterprise margins. This secondary economic multiplier effect is an unintended but positive outcome of the direct income transfer design.

The scheme also has relevance for women in families that rely heavily on seasonal income from horticulture, particularly apple farming in the upper hills; during the winter off-season when horticulture income is nil and agricultural wage work is unavailable, the guaranteed monthly transfer provides a reliable consumption floor for these households. The ability to count on Rs 1,500 regardless of the apple harvest outcome reduces the financial anxiety associated with agricultural income volatility in mountain farming systems.

extra_sections.title: Payment Not Received This Month?
extra_sections.content:
First check that your Aadhaar is still seeded to your bank account, since a broken link is the most common cause.

Then contact the Tehsil Welfare Officer or the state helpline with your application number to track and fix the issue.

extra_sections.heading: How the Payment Reaches You
content: State government data from the initial phase of the scheme showed rapid uptake in districts with higher concentrations of rural women in the target age group, with districts like Kangra, Mandi, and Hamirpur recording particularly large numbers of registrations; these are also districts with relatively better connectivity and Anganwadi infrastructure, which facilitated faster processing. The government has continued to extend registration drives to more remote areas to ensure equitable geographic coverage across all twelve districts of Himachal Pradesh.

As a scheme that delivers a recurring income entitlement to women, the Pyari Behna Sukh Samman Nidhi represents a structural approach to women's financial security rather than a one-time benefit; the sustained monthly transfer over years can contribute meaningfully to household savings, improved nutrition, and children's education in recipient families. The scheme's long-term social impact will depend on continued state budget allocation and on ensuring that eligible women in remote areas are not left out of the beneficiary list due to documentation or connectivity barriers.

extra_sections.text: The Indira Gandhi Pyari Behna Sukh Samman Nidhi Yojana delivers Rs 1,500 every month directly to the bank accounts of eligible women in Himachal Pradesh, creating a steady personal income stream that belongs entirely to the woman herself.

extra_sections.heading: How the Payment Reaches You More
content: One significant secondary effect of the scheme has been an increase in women's visits to banking facilities, which has in turn improved their familiarity with banking services such as recurring deposits, insurance-linked savings accounts, and digital payment tools. Block-level banking correspondents have reported a noticeable rise in women opening accounts and making transactions in areas where the Pyari Behna payment is the primary reason for their bank account activity, suggesting that the scheme is building financial literacy as a by-product of the income transfer.

The scheme's implementation in tribal belts of Himachal Pradesh, particularly in the inner line permit areas of Kinnaur and in the high-altitude villages of Lahaul and Spiti, has required additional logistical support because banking infrastructure in these areas is very sparse; the department has worked with the Himachal Pradesh Gramin Bank and state cooperative banks to extend BC services and mobile banking units to ensure payments reach women in these difficult geographies. In some cases, the nearest bank branch may be a day's journey away by road, making the mobile BC van the only realistic option for women to access their accounts.

extra_sections.heading: What Happens at Age 60
content: The age ceiling of 59 years for the Pyari Behna scheme was chosen deliberately to create a smooth transition to the state's social security pension for the elderly, which covers women from age 60 onwards at a higher monthly rate; in this way, the two schemes together can provide continuous monthly support to a woman from age 18 through old age, filling what would otherwise be a gap in the social protection architecture of Himachal Pradesh. Women approaching the age of 60 are advised to begin their pension application process before crossing the age threshold to avoid any break in monthly income.

Widows in Himachal Pradesh who are between 18 and 59 years of age and who meet the income criterion are eligible for the Pyari Behna scheme in addition to any widow-specific assistance they may receive under other programmes; the state government has not created a separate window for widowed beneficiaries, as the scheme's universal age-and-income approach is designed to include all economically vulnerable women without requiring proof of specific social circumstances. This inclusive design means that a widow does not need to produce a husband's death certificate or any marital status document to register.

extra_sections.title: If a Payment Is Missed Notes
extra_sections.content: Women who were previously dependent on remittances from male family members working in the plains as migrant labourers have found that the Pyari Behna payment provides a measure of financial independence that reduces their vulnerability during periods when remittances are delayed or stop altogether; this is particularly relevant in Himachal Pradesh where reverse migration from cities during economic slowdowns can create sudden household income shocks. The guaranteed monthly government transfer has thus provided a form of economic resilience that private labour market incomes cannot always ensure.

extra_sections.title: What Happens at Age 60 Notes
extra_sections.content:
The Rs 1,500 monthly transfer has also been noted by nutritionists and public health workers in Himachal Pradesh as having a potential impact on maternal and child nutrition in beneficiary households, as women who control income are statistically more likely to spend it on food, healthcare, and children's education than on other goods; while no formal impact study has yet been published on the Pyari Behna scheme specifically, the evidence base from similar schemes in other Indian states suggests positive nutritional outcomes over a 2-3 year period. The Women and Child Development Department has expressed interest in tracking nutritional outcomes in beneficiary households through its Anganwadi monitoring systems.

From a fiscal perspective, the Himachal Pradesh government has allocated dedicated funds for the Pyari Behna scheme in successive state budgets since the scheme's launch; the total annual outlay depends on the number of verified beneficiaries and has grown as registration has expanded to cover more eligible women. The scheme is financed entirely from the state's own tax revenues without central government matching funds, reflecting Himachal Pradesh's policy choice to prioritise women's income security as a core state expenditure even under fiscal constraints that the state routinely faces as a hill state with a high revenue expenditure burden.

extra_sections.heading: If a Payment Is Missed More
content: Himachal Pradesh's Women and Child Development Department has also emphasised the digital aspects of scheme delivery, encouraging beneficiaries to use the BHIM UPI app or Aadhaar Pay infrastructure to check their balance and make digital transactions with the funds they receive; this digital nudge is part of a broader state government goal of improving digital financial literacy among rural women. Over time, the department hopes that growing comfort with digital payment tools will open up additional economic opportunities for beneficiary women, including participation in online marketplaces for home-produced goods such as hand-knitted woolens, local jams, and hill produce that have strong urban demand.

The Pyari Behna scheme, in combination with schemes like the Mukhyamantri Swavalamban Yojana for self-employment and the HIMCARE health insurance programme, forms part of a comprehensive state-level social protection framework for women in Himachal Pradesh; taken together, these programmes address income security, health security, and livelihood promotion as interlocking dimensions of women's welfare. Eligible women are encouraged to explore all programmes they qualify for rather than treating the monthly income transfer as the only available form of state support.

faqs.question: What is the monthly amount given under Pyari Behna Sukh Samman Nidhi?
faqs.answer: Eligible women receive Rs 1,500 per month, credited directly to their Aadhaar-linked bank account through the DBT mechanism.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the Indira Gandhi Pyari Behna Sukh Samman Nidhi Yojana?
faqs.answer: Women aged 18 to 59 years who are residents of Himachal Pradesh and whose family's annual income is below Rs 2 lakh are eligible, provided they are not government employees, pensioners, or income tax payers.

faqs.question: When was the Pyari Behna scheme launched?
faqs.answer: The scheme was launched on February 25, 2024 by Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu.

faqs.question: Can a woman above 60 apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, the Pyari Behna Sukh Samman Nidhi is for women aged 18 to 59. Women aged 60 and above should check the HP Social Security Pension for elderly women.

faqs.question: Is this scheme for all castes and communities?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Pyari Behna scheme is open to all women in Himachal Pradesh within the age and income criteria, regardless of caste, religion, or community.

faqs.question: Where do I apply for the Pyari Behna scheme?
faqs.answer: You can apply at the nearest Block Development Office (BDO) or through the Anganwadi centre in your area. Anganwadi workers can help you fill the form.

faqs.question: What documents are needed to apply?
faqs.answer: You need an Aadhaar card, Himachal Pradesh domicile or residence certificate, income certificate from the Tehsildar showing family income below Rs 2 lakh, and a bank passbook for an account linked to Aadhaar.

faqs.question: Is a government employee's wife eligible for this scheme?
faqs.answer: No. If the woman herself is a government employee or pensioner, she is ineligible. Additionally, if the family is liable to pay income tax, she is excluded from the scheme.

faqs.question: How is the Rs 1,500 payment made?
faqs.answer: The payment is made through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) and is credited directly to the beneficiary's Aadhaar-linked bank account each month.

faqs.question: What should I do if I do not receive the payment for a month?
faqs.answer: Wait a few extra days as processing timelines can vary within the month. If the payment is not received by mid-month, contact the Block Development Office or the district Women and Child Development office with your application reference number.
